The structure of nicotinamide is shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The nitrogen atom in the six-membered ring has one electron in an unhybridised p-orbital. This electron becomes delocalised, becoming part of a single delocalised system of electrons. This delocalised system also includes:

- electrons from the carbon atoms in the six-membered ring
- the two electrons in the $\pi$ bond of the $\text{C=O}$ group
- the two electrons in the lone pair on the nitrogen atom of the amide group.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State the number of delocalised electrons in one nicotinamide molecule.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Predict the $\text{H-N-H}$ bond angle in the $\text{NH}_2$ group in nicotinamide.

parts.label: (b)
(b)(i)
parts.text: Draw the structural formula of **E** in the box.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Give the name or formula of a suitable reagent for step 2.

(d)
parts.text:
Nicotinamide can be reduced to compound **X**.

{{figure:pdf_visual_04.png}}

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Identify a suitable reducing agent for this reaction.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Predict and explain the relative basicities of the $\text{NH}_2$ groups in phenylamine, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$, nicotinamide and compound **X**.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
The height of the M peak in a mass spectrum of nicotinamide is 80.

Calculate the expected height of the M+1 peak.
